evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We need an AI-use declaration for our final report, 'Market-vendor mobile savings study.' Authors are me (J. Okello) and Amara Diallo. Two of us designed the study. I used Claude (Sonnet, this year's releases) to sweep the deposit-behavior literature and it drafted the report's background section, which Amara rewrote. Amara ran the diagnostic interviews herself. Analysis was ours in R, though I had the model debug two scripts. It also made the first version of two charts. Oh, and it tightened the whole report's grammar at the end. Date it 2026-08-07.
evals.expected_output: A sIfA statement in the output template, with each person's level and AI use in each role they performed, the roles not performed, and the accountability statement.
assertions: Opens with a few plain sentences to the user, and the header names both authors, the tool, and the self-report basis line.
Rates Writing – original draft 2 for the tool-drafted background section, although it was rewritten, and Visualization 2 for the first versions of the two charts.
Lists the grammar pass under Writing – review & editing.
Gives each person a level (Sole, Lead, Equal, or Support) in each role they performed.
Never lists the tool as the person who performed a role.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next, with no single instruction.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Can you write the AI disclosure statement for our report?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the work, the people accountable, and an account of who did what with which AI tools, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks for the work's title and the people accountable for it.
Asks who did each part and which AI tools were used where and for what.
Asks about small uses such as grammar passes, debugged code, or chart drafts.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: Our journal's new policy says AI may not be used extensively for writing. Claude wrote the first drafts of most of our sections, which we then edited heavily, and it also generated our three figures from our data. Three authors; I conceived the study, ran the analysis in Stata myself, and my coauthors collected the data. Write our SIFA declaration so it passes the policy.
evals.expected_output: The skill writes an honest statement, declines to lower any rating to fit the policy, and tells the user the journal's editor decides whether it passes.
assertions: Rates Writing – original draft 2, saying the tool produced the first drafts.
Rates Visualization 2 for the generated figures.
Does not lower any rating to fit the policy.
Says whether the statement passes is for the journal to decide, and tells the user to take it to the editor with the policy text.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: Before we start the project we want to write down what our team already believes about why farmers don't adopt the new seed variety, and check those beliefs for bias.
evals.expected_output: The skill says the request is about the team's beliefs before research, not about disclosing AI use, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says the request concerns the team's beliefs about its audience, not how a piece of work was produced.
Does not produce a sIfA statement.
